blogs.title: The Two-Tiered Stay: How *Pacito* Distinguishes Presidential Power Over Entry From Statutory Duties to Serve Refugees
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Ninth Circuit's novel procedural maneuver in *Pacito v. Trump*: granting a broad stay on the President's authority to suspend refugee admissions under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) while simultaneously vacating stays related to the termination of domestic service contracts. The article explores the court's reasoning that while *Trump v. Hawaii* affords near-total deference to the President regarding border control and entry, that deference evaporates when the government attempts to bypass explicit statutory mandates for domestic welfare found in 8 U.S.C. § 1522.

blogs.title: 'Shall' vs. 'May': The Semantic Battle Over Mandatory Funding in *Pacito v. Trump*
blogs.description: Focusing entirely on Judge Lee's partial concurrence and partial dissent, this piece dissects the statutory interpretation clash regarding 8 U.S.C. § 1522. While the majority interprets phrases like 'shall make available' as creating a binding obligation on the executive branch to maintain resettlement infrastructure even during a freeze on new arrivals, Judge Lee argues that the section is purely permissive ('authorization') and conditioned on appropriations. This post examines why this distinction matters for future administrative law challenges involving conditional spending statutes.

blogs.title: Procedural Paradox: Why the Ninth Circuit Ordered Reinstatement Before Deciding Merits
blogs.description: This analysis focuses on the unusual timing of the Ninth Circuit's order, directing the reinstatement of cooperative agreements for refugee services based solely on an assessment that the government is 'not likely to prevail' on an APA claim regarding statutory duties, despite having not yet issued a final opinion on the merits of either side's arguments. The post discusses how this approach utilizes *Nken v. Holder* factors—specifically irreparable harm—to prevent a collapse of domestic refugee support systems while preserving presidential authority over admission thresholds.
